questions.prompt: Where should you look first when a non-GUI run behaves oddly?
options: jmeter.log
The .jmx file's XML
The Windows event log
The HTML report's colour legend
questions.explanation: jmeter.log records script errors, missing classes and warnings. The others rarely explain JMeter-side problems.

questions.prompt: Which scripting option is recommended for performance?
options: JSR223 with Groovy and script caching
BeanShell
JavaScript in If Controllers
Running external shell scripts per sample
questions.explanation: Groovy with caching compiles once and runs fast. The others are slower.

questions.prompt: Increasing JMeter's heap beyond the machine's free RAM will make tests more stable.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A heap larger than available RAM causes swapping or failures. Size the heap well under the physical memory.

questions.prompt: Many samples fail with `java.net.SocketException: Connection reset` at high load, but the app logs show no errors. What do you check?
options: Load balancer/proxy limits, server connection backlogs and keep-alive timeouts between JMeter and the app
The JMeter GUI theme
The CSV file encoding
The Constant Timer value
questions.explanation: Resets usually come from network components or server connection limits. Unrelated settings will not fix them.

questions.prompt: What does 'Non HTTP response code: java.net.BindException' on Windows usually indicate?
options: The load generator ran out of ephemeral ports
The server returned 500
The CSV file is missing
A JSON path is wrong
questions.explanation: BindException means the client could not bind a local port, typically ephemeral port exhaustion. Keep-alive and tuning the port range help.

questions.prompt: Which reduce memory use on the load generator? Select all that apply.
options: Do not save response data in the JTL
Disable View Results Tree and Aggregate Graph during load
Use CSV JTL output rather than XML
Add a Debug Sampler to every iteration
questions.explanation: Response data, heavy listeners and XML output all consume memory. Debug Samplers add samples and should be disabled.

questions.prompt: A plan works in GUI on the laptop but non-GUI on the CI agent logs `FileNotFoundException: data\users.csv`. The agent runs Linux. What is the most likely fix?
options: Use forward slashes or a relative path built per OS (data/users.csv); backslashes are not path separators on Linux
Increase the heap
Install the Plugins Manager on CI
Run in GUI mode on CI
questions.explanation: Windows-style separators break on Linux. Heap, plugins and GUI mode are unrelated.

questions.prompt: Your first 3 minutes always show high response times, then results stabilise. How should you treat that period?
options: As warm-up (JIT, caches, connection pools): exclude it from the SLA analysis or run a warm-up phase before measuring, and report it separately
Delete the first 3 minutes from the JTL without mentioning it
Ignore warm-up entirely; it is never relevant
Add a Constant Timer at the start
questions.explanation: Warm-up is real but distinct from steady state. Excluding it transparently, or having an explicit warm-up phase, keeps analysis honest. Silently deleting data is misleading.

coding.title: Triage jmeter.log
coding.prompt: Write `triage(log_text)` returning a dict `{'ERROR': n, 'WARN': m, 'top': message}` where `n`/`m` count lines whose level field is `ERROR`/`WARN`, and `top` is the most common ERROR message (text after `: ` following the logger name), or `None`. Line format: `2026-11-12 10:00:01,123 ERROR o.a.j.t.JMeterThread: Test failed!`. On ties pick the message seen first.
coding.explanation: Counting by level and grouping messages points you at the dominant problem in a long log. `max` over a dict keeps the first key on ties because dicts preserve insertion order.
hints: Split each line into date, time, level, logger and message.
Use `max(msgs, key=msgs.get)` for the most common message.

tests.name: Counts
tests.code:
log = '2026-11-12 10:00:01,123 ERROR o.a.j.t.JMeterThread: Test failed!
2026-11-12 10:00:02,000 WARN o.a.j.s.FileServer: slow
2026-11-12 10:00:03,000 ERROR o.a.j.p.h.s.HTTPSampler: Connection reset
2026-11-12 10:00:04,000 ERROR o.a.j.p.h.s.HTTPSampler: Connection reset
2026-11-12 10:00:05,000 INFO o.a.j.e.StandardJMeterEngine: Running'
assert triage(log) == {'ERROR': 3, 'WARN': 1, 'top': 'Connection reset'}

tests.name: No errors
tests.code: assert triage('2026-11-12 10:00:05,000 INFO o.a.j.e.X: ok') == {'ERROR': 0, 'WARN': 0, 'top': None}

coding.title: Choose a safe heap size
coding.prompt:
Write `heap_setting(total_ram_gb, other_usage_gb)` returning the `HEAP` value string. Use 70% of `(total_ram_gb - other_usage_gb)`, rounded **down** to whole GB, capped at 31 GB, and at least 1 GB. Use the same value for `-Xms` and `-Xmx`.

Example: `heap_setting(16, 2)` returns `'-Xms9g -Xmx9g'`.
coding.solution:
import math

def heap_setting(total_ram_gb, other_usage_gb):
    gb = math.floor((total_ram_gb - other_usage_gb) * 0.7)
    gb = max(1, min(31, gb))
    return f'-Xms{gb}g -Xmx{gb}g'
coding.explanation: Leaving headroom for the OS and other processes avoids swapping, and staying under about 32 GB keeps compressed object pointers. Equal min and max avoids heap resizing during the run.
hints: Compute the free RAM, then 70% of it.
Clamp between 1 and 31 with `max(1, min(31, x))`.
